title: trailboss --json team show
description: One team: what `team show <name>` gives, and `team trust <name>` too (its `trust` then trusted with --yes). Each repository agent definition a role names still needs its own trust, shown as the role's problem.

name.description: What `team start` and `team show` take: the file's name without `.json`, or a built-in team's name.

source.description: repo (the repository's `.trailboss/teams/`), user (`~/.config/trailboss/teams/`) or built-in. A name from an earlier source wins.

path.description: The team's file; null when built in.

active.description: Whether this is the one its name starts: false when a team earlier in repo, user, built-in order has the same name.

trust.description: A repository team's trust: trusted, new or changed (since you trusted it). Null for yours and built-in ones, which need none.

lead.description: The lead's role; null when the file couldn't be read.

dollars.description: The most the team may spend, in dollars: the file's, else 20; null when the file couldn't be read.

hours.description: The most hours it may run: the file's, else 4.

members.description: The most members of all its roles together, the lead included.

problem.description: Why it can't be used; null when it can.

lead.description: Whether it's the lead's role: its one member is the lead `team start --yes` starts.

agent.description: The agent definition its members start from (`agents ls`).

works.description: How its members work: task (its own git worktree and branch, started with `task add --role`), review (one of the team's tasks, with `task review --role`) or shared-readonly (in the team's folder, to read and plan, with `start --role`); more may be added.

count.description: The most members of it that may start, over the team's whole run.

description.description: What its members do, from the team file.

kind.description: The agent kind the definition starts: claude, codex, …; null when it has a problem.

source.description: Where the definition comes from: repo, user or built-in; null when it has a problem.

path.description: The definition's file; null for a built-in one.

trust.description: A repository definition's trust (always trusted when resolved); null for yours and built-in ones.

command.description: What a member runs, its brief shown as `<brief>`; null when it has a problem.

problem.description: Why the definition can't start as things are (unknown, broken, a repository's not trusted); null when it can.

roles.description: Each role, its definition resolved from the folder as `task add` and `start` would resolve it.

file.description: The team file as read: description, lead, roles and limits.
